newsitem.title: UK: Further liberalisation of Mexico oil, gas unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Further liberalisation of Mexico oil, gas unlikely.

text.p: The prospects for further liberalisation of Mexico's oil and gas industry remain slim for the foreseeable future, an official said on Monday.

Jorge Navarrete, Mexico's under-secretary for energy told an industry conference substantial alterations to the current legal framework which maintains the State's monopoly in the production, refining and processing of oil and gas were unlikely in the short-term.
"There is no strong probability during the present administration that runs to the year 2000," Navarrete said.
Mexico produced 2.8 million barrels per day of oil in 1996 with half heading for export. The U.S accounted for 70 percent of the exports.

In 1992 Mexico began opening up electricity generation to private investors at home and abroad and in 1995 the law was changed to allow private participation in the transport, storage and distribution of natural gas.
Navarrete said future hydro-carbon exploration activity would focus on three projects in the Campeche Gulf, Tabasco coastline and the Borges basin,
In the downstream sector investments would be linked to improving quality of products from existing refineries to meet tighter environmental standards.

Navarrete said no new refinery would be built this century, but that money would be spent to improve fuel oil conversion rates at the Tula and Cadereyta refineries of State-owned Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
He was speaking at the annual Centre for Global Energy Studies conference.
